name: @mica/sdk
//files: MICA-125. Consumed as source, so the tarball ships source: every .ts, .svelte and .css, minus the suites. Without this it shipped 324 files including 58 tests. Widen it rather than narrowing if a consumer build ever fails to resolve something — a file missing here is an error only the consumer sees.
//: MICA-172. Consumed as source: the phone and every add-on bundle build this package through their own Vite pipeline, so there is no build step and no `main`. `@mica/sdk/testing` is deliberately absent, because it resolves to `web/src/testing.ts` — a phone helper, not published contract (see `publicSurface.test.ts`). It stays an alias on the web side.
//exports: MICA-125: `.` is `addon.ts`, the add-on barrel, not `index.ts`. The bare specifier is inherently target-dependent — in this repo the shell build and the add-on build alias it to different files — so the map can only be right for one audience, and the audience that reads the map is the one outside this repo, which is add-on authors. `index.ts` is the shell's barrel and is published under no subpath at all: the shell always has a Vite config to alias in, and an outside consumer resolving it would get six names it cannot call and no `bootAddOn`. Nothing in this repo resolves through this map — every in-tree consumer aliases past it — which is what made the switch safe to make. `publicSurface.test.ts` holds the map and the frozen surfaces against each other in both directions.
//peerDependencies: MICA-125. Svelte and Vite are the consumer's to supply, not this package's to bring. `bootAddOn` calls `mount()` (`host/iframe/boot.ts`) and 85 components are compiled by whoever builds them, so a consumer that resolves its own Svelte gets two copies, two component registries and two sets of context keys — a bug whose symptom is a component that renders and then silently stops reacting, with nothing in any error to name the cause. The floors are what the toolchain that compiles this package already enforces: `@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte@7` declares `svelte: ^5.46.4` and `vite: ^8.0.0` itself, so a lower version of either cannot build these components in the supported configuration. Both stay in `devDependencies` at the versions this repo builds with — a peer is a requirement on the consumer and installs nothing here, and `svelte-check`, `eslint-plugin-svelte` and this package's own suite all need them resolvable from `sdk/`.
